subject.title: Background PTY exec runs can survive restart/session loss and become untracked orphan process trees

question: Should stale PTY-backed background exec runs from a previous gateway epoch be killed on startup, reattached/re-registered, or left to in-process reconciliation only?
rationale: Current source proves the ownership gap, but the durable restart behavior changes semantics for legitimate long-running background work and must be an explicit maintainer lifecycle policy.

options.title: Kill previous-epoch PTY runs
options.body: Persist active PTY ownership and terminate stale previous-epoch trees during startup reconciliation, with logs and tests for normal finalize cleanup.

options.title: Reattach stale PTY runs
options.body: Persist enough metadata to re-register surviving runs after restart, accepting more state and platform-specific validation to preserve long-running work.

options.title: Ship in-process mitigation only
options.body: Use the linked PR's session-registry reconciliation as a partial fix while leaving cold-start orphan cleanup unresolved and tracked here.

recommendation.title: Kill previous-epoch PTY runs
recommendation.body: Persist active PTY ownership and terminate stale previous-epoch trees during startup reconciliation, with logs and tests for normal finalize cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the deepest background exec history and introduced the background-session behavior whose restart lifecycle is being decided.
